answer: Resource slot fingerprinting ties each agent identity to a distinct draw from a public schedule. Requests must present matching timing and entropy traces; duplicates sharing a backend reveal themselves when their traces collide on a trellis slot. Collisions freeze the cluster’s access and forfeit its prepaid nectar allotment. An attacker must pay separate hardware, network, and entropy costs per identity, plus an umber deposit that is lost on any detected duplicate.
